newsitem.title: CHINA: China '97 foreign investment seen at $49.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: China '97 foreign investment seen at $49.5 bln.

text.p: Direct foreign investment in China was expected to reach $49.5 billion in 1997, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
China should attract actual investments of about $40 billion this year, central bank governor Dai Xianglong has said.
Actual foreign investment reached $29.2 billion in the first nine months, according to the official media.
More investment would go to China's less developed central and western regions because of state policies designed to speed development in these laggard areas, the Financial News said.
The proportion of investment from Hong Kong would rise because of the return of the British colony to Beijing rule next year, the newspaper said.
More multi-national companies would invest in China and boost the scale of individual projects. More investment was expected in property development.
The report also urged the government to give preferential treatment to foreign investors in China's agriculture, power and communication sectors but curb investment in labour-intensive industries.
